entries.name: $JP2DOS
entries.purpose: return to TRSDOS READY

entries.name: $CMDTXT
entries.purpose: start of the buffer holding the last command line typed at TRSDOS READY

entries.name: $FILPTR
entries.purpose: get the drive and logical file number of an open file

entries.name: $RAMDIR
entries.purpose: copy directory entries, or the free-space figure, into a RAM buffer

entries.name: $COMDOS
entries.purpose: run a TRSDOS command line, then return to TRSDOS READY

entries.name: $CMDDOS
entries.purpose: run a TRSDOS command line and return to the caller

entries.name: $ERRDSP
entries.purpose: display the TRSDOS error message for the code in A

entries.name: $MEMEND
entries.purpose: highest memory address available, low byte first; normally the end of RAM

entries.name: $DSPDIR
entries.purpose: display the directory of the non-protected files on one drive

entries.name: $SYNTAX
entries.purpose: check a file specification and copy it into a DCB

entries.name: $INIT
entries.purpose: open a file, creating it if it does not exist

entries.name: $OPEN
entries.purpose: open an existing file

entries.name: $CLOSE
entries.purpose: close an open file

entries.name: $KILL
entries.purpose: delete a file and release its disk space

entries.name: $READ
entries.purpose: read a record from an open file

entries.name: $WRITE
entries.purpose: write a record to an open file

entries.name: $VERF
entries.purpose: write a record, then read it back and compare

entries.name: $REWIND
entries.purpose: point a file back at its first record

entries.name: $POSN
entries.purpose: position a file at a given logical record

entries.name: $BKSPC
entries.purpose: back up one record in a file
entries.note: the list of routines on page 78 spells this $BACKSPACE; its heading on page 82 and the index entry BKSPC (82) spell it $BKSPC

entries.name: $POSEOF
entries.purpose: point a file at its last record, to extend it

entries.name: $PUTEXT
entries.purpose: add an extension to a filename that has none

entries.name: $DMULT
entries.purpose: multiply a 16-bit value by an 8-bit multiplier: 24-bit product in H, L, and A

entries.name: $DIVIDE
entries.purpose: divide a 16-bit value by an 8-bit divisor: quotient in HL, remainder in A
